product_contract.ci_hygiene: The scanner is read-only, creates no temporary files, and detects stale exceptions so policy debt cleans up after retired files.
product_contract.cloud_native: Exceptions must point toward Rust cloud-ci, Kubernetes, GitOps, controller, or admission-policy replacements.
product_contract.execution: Buck2-native Rust gate; no Cargo command is required for enforcement.
product_contract.portability: Policy is data-driven so another repository can adopt the same gate by changing scan roots and exceptions.

purpose: Rust-first automation hygiene ratchet. Non-Rust scripts are blocked unless explicitly exceptioned as shrinkable debt with a Rust/Buck2/cloud-native replacement path.

workflow_inline_shell._comment: pipeline-glue(a): the file-extension scan above is blind to shell that lives INSIDE workflow YAML `run:` steps (the file is `.yml`, not `.sh`). This dimension parses the declared workflow roots with a real YAML parser, emits one keyed observation per (file, job, step) carrying an inline `run:` block, and ratchets it shrink-only against the frozen keyed baseline face rust-first-automation-workflow-shell-baseline.json. New inline shell beyond baseline is born-blocking; a retired step must shrink the baseline in the same PR. Removing the shell itself (productizing it as a Rust/Buck2 step) is pipeline-glue(b).

workflow_forbidden_uses._comment: Forbid third-party / marketplace Buck2 setup actions. The allowed bridge is repo-owned infra/ci/install-buck2.sh, which downloads the official facebook/buck2 release asset and verifies the pinned SHA-256 before execution.

interpreter_command_authority._comment: G006 inventory-first guard: Rust automation/gate source must not re-authorize retired Python/Node/MJS authority by spawning interpreter commands directly. The scan is intentionally scoped to automation/gate code; cloud/cloud-os is owned by the later kernel/OS story and is excluded from this task-4 lane.

workflow_inline_shell_baseline._comment: FROZEN keyed baseline of TODAY's accepted legacy-bridge inline shell inside GitHub workflow YAML `run:` steps (pipeline-glue(a)). The file-extension scan (scan.non_rust_extensions over scan.roots) counts non-Rust automation FILES and is structurally blind to shell INSIDE a `.yml` (the file is a `.yml`, not a `.sh`). The scan.workflow_inline_shell dimension closes that blind spot: it parses the declared workflow roots with a real YAML parser and emits one keyed observation per (file, job, step) carrying an inline `run:` block. This baseline freezes that surface SHRINK-ONLY. Each key is `<workflow-relpath>::<job-id>::step-<N>` (N = 0-based step index within the job's `steps` array) -- the finest defensible per-(file,job,step) unit. The live-repo gate test asserts the MEASURED inline-shell key set equals codes.rust_first_automation_unbaselined_workflow_inline_shell EXACTLY (set equality): a NEW inline `run:` step beyond this baseline is born-blocking (rust_first_automation_unbaselined_workflow_inline_shell), a RETIRED step must shrink the baseline in the SAME PR (rust_first_automation_workflow_inline_shell_baseline_stale). Folded INTO this policy (an already-accounted gate face) rather than a new sibling JSON so adding the baseline creates ZERO new tracked accounting rows (no firewall ratchet growth). NOT producer-regenerated -- reviewed, hand-shrunk; anti-laundering is REVIEW-VISIBLE. REMOVING the shell itself (productizing each step as a Rust/Buck2 step) is pipeline-glue(b). FRIC-017 (pipeline-glue(b)): the two duplicated multi-line `sudo rm -rf` disk-reclaim blocks (buck2::step-4, gate-affected-set::step-4) are PRODUCTIZED -- each is now a single irreducible-glue `buck2 run` invocation of the data-driven Rust preflight oya-cloud-ci-runner-disk-reclaim-bin (policy: cloud/cloud-ci/gates/oya-cloud-ci-runner-disk-reclaim-app/runner-disk-reclaim-policy.json). The 1:1 step swap keeps the SAME (file,job,step) keys (the invocation step stays at index 4 in each job), so the keyed baseline is UNCHANGED -- the productization shrinks the inline-shell LINE footprint (6 `run:` lines -> 1) while the residual keys are baselined as accepted irreducible runner-bootstrap glue. The FRIC-017 ledger row is flipped to fixed-in-PR; the terminal claim is contingent on CI green on the real runner (PR pending merge). #101 live-Postgres lane (gate-live-postgres::step-2..6, +5 keys, oya-ci-required 32->37 / total 52->57): the durable cross-tenant-deny / RLS / CDC / SCIM integration tests are inherently NON-hermetic (they require an external containerized Postgres reachable over the network), so they run via `cargo test` as a TRANSITIONAL BRIDGE until a buck2 rust_test action declares the disposable DB as a managed local_resource (testcontainers-style ephemeral env); the toolchain-provision / apt-install-psql / migration-bootstrap / cargo-test steps are baselined as accepted irreducible bridge glue until that cloud-native runner exists. Step indices are 2..6 (not 1..5) because step-1 is the Swatinem/rust-cache `uses:` step (no `run:` block, not keyed), shifting all subsequent run: steps by +1 (review #806 fix-3).

The gate matrix adds one reviewed inline-shell key for the repo-owned official-Buck2 installer plus the Buck2 test step (gate::step-2..4). The live-Postgres lane replaces Swatinem rust-cache and cargo test with repo-owned install-buck2, actions/cache toolchain warmup, and buck2 test --local-only against the job's Postgres service; current live-Postgres keys are step-1 and step-3..7.
